observations: Photos show a framed solar panel (front view with many cells; no clear wattage label visible).
Photo 2 shows the back of the panel; no readable brand/model/wattage sticker visible.
Photo 3 shows the back again; still no readable rating/serial plate visible.
Seller text talks about a battery (new, holds charge for 8 hours), but the photos appear to be only a solar panel.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours.
claims.evidence: No battery is shown in the provided photos; only a solar panel is visible.
No battery condition/inspection photos (or any battery) are provided to verify repair history.
Seller’s general business statement; photos do not confirm what exact item is being sold.

risks.risk: Item mismatch: seller claims battery performance, but photos show only a solar panel.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the actual battery being sold (front label with brand/model, capacity/voltage, and a close-up of terminals).
risks.if_unproven: Price as a solar panel only (battery claims ignored) and treat as worst-case unknown wattage/condition.

risks.risk: Wattage/brand/model not readable from photos, so the correct comparable price cannot be matched confidently.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear close-up photo of the panel’s rating label (watts, Voc, Isc, brand, model/serial).
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest matching comparable for an unspecified/possibly lower-watt panel.

risks.risk: Panel condition not verifiable remotely (cracks, micro-cracks, delamination, water ingress).
risks.proof: Ask for close-ups of the glass surface corners and cell grid, plus a photo of the frame for dents; ideally an IV curve/test reading.
risks.if_unproven: Assume not tested/unknown performance and price at the lowest end of the comparable range.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up of the solar panel rating plate/sticker showing watts (W), brand, model, and serial number (photo 0/1/2/3 close-up).
Confirm whether the sale is for a battery, a solar panel, or a full package; send photos of the battery if it’s included (label + terminals).
Provide a test proof for the panel (IV curve reading or a meter test) and for the battery (capacity/voltage reading and a discharge test result).
response.reason: The seller’s key claims are about a battery, but the photos show only a solar panel and the panel’s wattage/brand/model are not readable. Without the rating label (and without a battery photo if included), a safe price match is not possible.
